newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek yield curve frozen in quiet trade.
newsitem.headline: Greek yield curve frozen in quiet trade.

text.p: Greek money, bond and forex markets were calm in early trade with rates holding Wednesday closing levels, and dealers said they expected no changes today with U.S markets closed and a 24-hour general strike in Greece.

"There is very little trading activity so far and rates are stuck at Wednesday levels," said a foreign bank dealer. "There is talk that the central bank will cut its overnight intervention rate and reports of lower November inflation."
But other dealers said the central bank would not cut its intervention rate soon unless it came under pressure from the government.

Greek daily Imerisia reports today that National Economy and Finance Minister Yannos Papandoniou predicted that CPI inflation would fall to 7.9 percent year-on-year in November from 8.3 percent in October.
The mark was quoted at 157.25/35 drachmas from Thursday's 157.260 fix, the dollar at 240.26/36 drachmas from 239.920 and the Ecu at 303.14/24 from 303.160 drachmas.
